explanation: This effect, electromagnetic induction, is how the generators in most power stations work. Faraday, a blacksmith's son with little schooling, started out as a bookbinder's apprentice.

claims.text: In 1831 Michael Faraday discovered electromagnetic induction: moving a magnet near a coil of wire makes electricity flow in the coil.
Alessandro Volta died in 1827, Benjamin Franklin in 1790, and Thomas Edison was born in 1847, so none of them made this 1831 discovery.
Most power stations generate electricity with generators that work by electromagnetic induction.
Faraday was the son of a blacksmith and had little formal schooling.
Faraday began his working life as an apprentice to a bookbinder.
